Anya (support): Raised by Acme: multiple 524/timeout + auth failures when calling /v1/streams. Requests show 300-600ms to edge but 800-1500ms to origin, and some 401s. Customer claims region=eu-west-1 but traffic hitting us-east-1.

Leo (eng-infra): Can you paste request headers (redact api key)? Need Host, x-redwood-region, X-Forwarded-For, x-envoy-original-path, x-envoy-decorator-operation.

Anya (support): Pasted sample (redacted):
```
:authority: api.redwood.ai
:method: POST
:path: /v1/streams
x-api-key: REDACTED
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
host: api.redwood.ai
x-forwarded-for: 34.12.5.6
```
They also ran curl from eu-west-1:
```
curl -v -H "x-api-key: REDACTED" -H "x-redwood-region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
```
Response headers included `x-served-region: us-east-1` and `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 1120`.

Mina (eng-runtime): Hmm. That `x-served-region` is set by the L7 gateway routing filter. We added a fallback rule that rewrites region header when route is missing. Possible bug where header rewrite uses last-match instead of route match. Repro steps?

Anya (support): Customer logs show intermittent auth 401s for the same token when the request goes to us-east-1 — they have org locked to eu models, so token validation fails in the other region. Sequence: 1) request with x-redwood-region: eu-west-1 2) edge returns 200 but server responds 401 from origin 3) later requests to eu work.

Leo (eng-infra): I'm pushing a debug envoy config with extra logging to the gateway cluster. @deploy-bot starting canary with log-level=trace on gw-v2 in us-east-1,eu-west-1.

deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy gw-v2 -> instances: gw-v2-canary-03 (eu-west-1). Rollout id: r-20260317-11 :rotating_light: 

Mina (eng-runtime): Quick check — are we accidentally copying `x-redwood-region` into `x-envoy-original-dst` or rewriting host header? There was one recent change to upstream cluster selection where we set `route.metadata.match` fallback to `any`.

Leo (eng-infra): Found a config diff: envoy route has `request_headers_to_add` that sets `x-served-region` using `%UPSTREAM_REGION%` but the variable is coming from the last configured cluster rather than matched cluster. That matches symptoms.

Anya (support): Customer wants a mitigation ASAP. They see failed invoices due to retries and some throughput loss.

Mina (eng-runtime): Mitigation: add explicit header removal + correct header set on route match. I can push a hotfix to canary, backfill to prod if tests pass. Also propose a short TTL cache purge for routing decisions.

Leo (eng-infra): I prepared a patch (envoy route template change). I'll roll to eu-west canary now. If no errors in 10m, promote to us-east and then prod.

Mina (eng-runtime): Patch details:
```
- request_headers_to_add:
  - header:
      key: x-served-region
      value: "%UPSTREAM_REGION%"
+ request_headers_to_add:
+  - header:
+      key: x-served-region
+      value: "%ROUTE_MATCH_CLUSTER_REGION%"
```
(Using the explicit route var)

Anya (support): After canary, customer confirmed 10 consecutive requests from eu low-latency and no 401s. :tada: 

Leo (eng-infra): I'll follow up with postmortem. Need to add test to e2e for header rewrite and region-locking auth. Also add monitoring alert when x-served-region != x-redwood-region for >1% of requests.

Mina (eng-runtime): Agreed. Adding backfill work item to eng-runtime backlog. Tagging incident-bot for severity 3 follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-20260317-12 severity: S3 owner: Mina (eng-runtime) link: https://redwood.atlassian/INC-20260317-12

Anya (support): Closing the customer's escalation; will keep them updated. Thanks all. :heart:
